query: What signals indicate a hardware incident is in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorising incidents (software/hardware/etc.) is directly relevant to isolating hardware incidents, giving a clean grouping axis. Values are well-grounded in short_description (e.g. 'MySQL server'->database, 'software installation'->software). Slight redundancy risk with the existing 'category' column caps usefulness, but it still enables the hardware filter the query needs.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Failure mode (connection_failure, crash, overheating, not_turning_on) is a strong signal axis for characterising hardware incidents and is exactly the kind of new dimension the query asks about. Values track the source text well (connection to MySQL -> connection_failure) and NULL for silent rows is acceptable behaviour.

per_column.name: symptom_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: A symptom/severity axis can help profile anomaly-window signals. However values partly overlap with failure_mode (malfunction/crash/performance_degradation) making it a partial restatement, and some labels like 'malfunction_unresponsive' on a plain 'software installation' request are not clearly warranted by the source text, indicating occasional over-assertion.

per_column.name: resolution_lag_band
per_column.rationale: Resolution lag is highly relevant to detecting anomaly windows and gives a real modelling axis. But groundedness is weak: in every evidence sample sys_updated_on equals closed_at and no opened_at is shown, so a 'same_day' outcome is implied, yet the produced bands (four_to_seven_days, eight_to_fourteen_days) contradict the visible timestamps, suggesting values not supported by the shown text.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual_device, server_room, building) is a genuinely useful blast-radius axis for anomaly analysis. Some values are warranted (MySQL server -> shared_resource), but assigning 'individual_device' to a bare 'software installation' request is a confident specific the text does not support.

per_column.name: opener_to_closer_match
per_column.rationale: A boolean comparing opener vs closer is derivable from existing caller_id/closed_by fields and offers only weak leverage for a hardware-anomaly query; it is largely a mechanical restatement of original columns rather than a new analytical axis.

per_column.name: software_update_related
per_column.rationale: A software-update flag is reasonably grounded ('Unable to install new update' -> True) but is essentially a narrow sub-slice of incident_category and, being software-focused, offers limited leverage for the hardware-incident query; a bare boolean flag adds modest analytical value.

judge.rationale: The set provides several genuinely useful new axes for characterising hardware incidents and anomaly windows (failure_mode, resolution_lag_band, affected_scope, incident_category), which is the core of the query. Weaknesses: symptom_severity_signal partly restates failure_mode, and the two booleans add limited leverage. Groundedness is mixed: category and failure-mode readings track the source text, but resolution_lag_band contradicts the visible identical timestamps, and affected_scope/severity sometimes assert specifics the text does not support, indicating occasional over-confident inference.
